name: Fuadijan Social Media & Marketing Strategy 2026–27
source: Strategy document of 2 Nov 2026 (Ahmad). Edit this file to change what the agent is told; numbers marked "verify" are not confirmed.
positioning: For families, students and halal food lovers across Western Sydney, Fuadijan is the Pakistani grill on Parramatta Road where BBQ and karahi are cooked fresh to order, portions are generous, and parking is easy.
oneIdea: Pakistani BBQ and karahi, made fresh to order, with family-size portions and easy parking.

knownFor.primary: Fresh-off-the-grill Pakistani BBQ (tikka, seekh, chapli) and made-to-order karahi.
knownFor.secondary: Generous, good-value family meals with no-stress parking.
knownFor.trust: 100% halal meat from certified suppliers — stated plainly, every time.

taglines.text: Fresh off the grill. Halal, always.
Karahi made the way it's made at home.
Big plates. Bigger flavour. Easy parking.

do: Make the grill the star: fire, char, steam, the wok being finished.
Say what is true and visible instead of adjectives: the spice blend, the cut of meat, the cooking time, the person cooking.
State the trust layer plainly: 100% halal meat from certified suppliers.
Say "fresh, grilled, halal" and "grilled not deep-fried, fresh meat, made to order" rather than "healthy".
Mention easy parking in every family post.
Point every post to direct ordering at fuadijan.com.au.
Keep the emotional arc "the taste of home, shared with everyone".
Australian English; warm, close, appetising; owner and staff faces regularly.
dont: Never lead with "healthy halal meals": it reads as a vague health claim and invites scepticism and consumer-law risk.
Never rely on "authentic" alone; it is what every competitor says.
Never say "halal certified" unless Fuadijan itself holds a certificate; say "100% halal meat from certified suppliers".
Never name a city (Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi) in a dish or story until the family roots are confirmed.
Never incentivise reviews, and never offer compensation publicly for editing one.
Never quote a review count or rating in an ad before re-checking the live Google numbers.

photoPrompts: Tikka skewers on the grill, flame rising behind, shallow depth of field.
Karahi in its wok on a dark table, steam lit from the side, coriander and ginger julienne on top.
Chapli kebab broken in half, showing the texture, tomato slice and pomegranate visible.
A tall glass of carrot or sugarcane juice, condensation on the glass, beside a plate from the grill.
Gulab jamun or kheer in a small bowl at the end of a table, the empty plates behind it.
Top-down family spread: two karahis, platter, naan basket, raita, salad, six hands reaching in.
Burger cross-section with cheese pull, on brown paper.
Owner portrait at the grill, warm light, looking at the food not the camera.
Exterior at golden hour with the car park visible.
Naan coming out of the oven, close-up on blistering.
Spice tray: whole spices in small bowls, top-down.
Students around a table with a large karahi and drinks.
photoRules: Motion beats stills: steam, sizzle, pour, pull-apart naan, chapli cracking.
Shoot at the pass, within 30 seconds of plating, before steam and gloss fade.
Side window light by day; one warm LED panel at 45° by night. Never overhead fluorescent alone.
45° for karahi and platters, top-down for spreads, macro for char on tikka.
Record grill sizzle and wok sounds clean.
Hands in frame: tearing naan, dipping in raita.
Batch film: one 90-minute session every Thursday prep + Friday service gives a week of content.

visual.palette: The kit's Night, Cream, Ember and Saffron carry every post; warm gold reads as Saffron. Deep green belongs to the halal promise, Ramadan, Eid and Pakistan Day posts only, and only as an accent.
rules: Warm, close, appetising: dark backgrounds, steam, char, hands breaking naan; a consistent warm grade.
Make the grill the star; the plate stays whole and the type stays big.
Real photos of the real dishes for anything that shows food sold; generated imagery only for backgrounds and mood.
Text on screen that TikTok search can read: Sydney, halal, Pakistani BBQ.

monthlyLoop: Pull numbers into the dashboard table (add a column per month).
Rank content: top 5 and bottom 5 posts by saves+shares and by Google/website clicks.
Keep, kill, test: double the formats in the top 5; drop the bottom 5 for a month; test one new format.
Check events: did each ritual beat its baseline? No lift after 6 weeks → change the offer or the night.
Read reviews: new themes, new complaints, fixes to announce.
Set next month: theme weeks, one event, one creator or community collaboration, posting quotas.
